newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst to sell unit, part of restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst to sell unit, part of restructuring.

text.p: German Hoechst AG, Europe's largest chemicals group, said on Tuesday it would sell its unit Asid Bonz GmbH to German group Willy Ruesch AG, as part of a broad restructuring in its drugs unit Hoechst Marion Roussel.
Asid Bonz, a hospital supplies provider, posted sales of 46 million marks ($29.8 million) in 1995.

Hoechst is in the process of restructuring its drugs unit as part of efforts to turn it into a separate legal entity. As part of the same plan, the group last week said it would buy the remaining stake of French drugs group Roussel-Uclaf that it did not own already. ($ = 1.545 German Marks)
